maria: Heads-up — competitor X just shipped 'cost-aware routing' in their hosted offering. Enterprise customers asking if we can match parity. Can we do a quick decision on scope?
raj: Noted. Can you paste the feature summary or link?
maria: link: https://x.example.com/blog/cost-aware-routing (shared internally). Key bits: policy-based routing by cost/latency, automatic fallback to cheaper model variants, per-tenant controls.
elena: From infra side, automatic fallback + per-tenant controls touches our routing layer and billing metrics. Need to know SLOs for fallback.
ash: @maria small correction — that's @ashley from sales flagged it earlier.
maria: Right — @ashley can explain which customers care and why.

maria: @trevor can you estimate infra impact for routing + fallback? This is prioritization-level — we might propose phased scope.
trevor: Rough sketch: Phase A (MVP) = routing policy engine + simple model-variant fallback in hosted only; minimal per-tenant config, default policy that prefers latency then cost. Phase B = per-tenant UI, canary rollout, Dedicated/Private support, telemetry hooks.
raj: Phase A risk: KV cache churn if fallback swaps models mid-request; could blow latency. Need to ensure we only fallback between compatible model architectures or on next request.
elena: Agree. Also instrumentation for token-level costs must be accurate before we let policy make decisions. Billing gap = dealbreaker for finance.
nash: Stop. This is getting silly.
nash: Why am I here.
maria: @raj, what's rough eng effort for Phase A? Months? Sprints?
raj: 6-8 engineer-weeks for core policy routing + api + lightweight telemetry. Another 3-4 weeks for robust metrics and canary hooks. That's optimistic.

maria: @elena any security/compliance blockers for per-tenant controls in hosted?
elena: Data plane stays the same; routing decisions don't require new data. However, Dedicated/Private needs control plane changes for safe config sync and KMS usage. That's Phase B.

maria: ok this thread is devolving. moving on. @ashley pls confirm customers and whether they're fine with hosted-only MVP. Also, product asks for success criteria:
- measurable cost savings >= 20% for targeted workloads
- no more than +5% p90 latency regression
- telemetry showing fallback rate and user impact
- GA only after 2 enterprise customers trial for 4 weeks

ash: (silence).
ash: test.

ashley: Customers asking: two fintechs + one marketplace. They want per-tenant controls and SLA for predictable cost. Fintechs require private deployment eventually but are ok with hosted pilot if SLA and audit logs are provided.
maria: Good. Decision proposal: 1) Approve Phase A MVP for Hosted only: policy engine, API, default safe fallback (no mid-request model swap), telemetry + billing accuracy. 2) Track Phase B (UI, Dedicated/Private, advanced policies) as separate epic with enterprise timeline. 3) Launch criteria = the 4 success bullets above.
raj: Engineering caveat: need gating item — billing accuracy. We should block rollout to paying customers until token-cost accounting matches finance within 2%.
trevor: Ops note: capacity planning — fallback could shift load to cheaper models but also create hot-spot for those models. Need autoscaling policy and a simulated load test.
elena: Compliance note: fintechs will need audit logs and config export; we'll scope that into Phase B but must have basic logging in Phase A.
maria: Next steps: @raj to draft tech spec with risks and rollback plan by EOD Friday, @trevor to run a capacity simulation plan, @ashley to confirm customers ok with hosted MVP and timelines. We'll reconvene Monday.
sonar-bot: tech-spec created: link internal/doc/competitive-routing-spec (uploaded by raj) :thumbsup:
raj: Uploaded draft. PTAL.
maria: Thanks everyone. If we get customer buy-in this looks like a medium-priority cross-team epic.
nash: stop. The end.
